text:
jordan: FYI — customer report: intermittent 504s when using our Go SDK v0.12.0. They see 'context canceled' and SDK retries. Repro steps + config below.

jordan: Code snippet from customer:
```go
client := &http.Client{
    Timeout: 30 * time.Second,
    Transport: &http.Transport{
        MaxIdleConns: 100,
        MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 10,
        IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
        TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
        ResponseHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
    },
}
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

jordan: Logs they sent:
```
2026-02-10T14:21:11Z error: request failed: net/http: request canceled
2026-02-10T14:21:11Z info: retrying (attempt 2) ...
2026-02-10T14:21:12Z warn: upstream returned 504 Gateway Timeout
```

eli: Can you confirm whether their ctx has a shorter deadline than ResponseHeaderTimeout? If ctx.Done triggers first, we get 'request canceled' and SDK still retries perhaps because it starts a new request with fresh context.

jordan: Customer says they set per-request ctx with 6s deadline. So ctx < ResponseHeaderTimeout (5s) actually ctx longer — wait they said backend sometimes takes 8-10s. Their ResponseHeaderTimeout is 5s -> that will cancel before header arrives and client reports canceled. That's likely.

priya: Also note MaxIdleConnsPerHost=10 might be too low under bursts; connections get reused, and when Transport hits ResponseHeaderTimeout it can leave connections in a state that confuses retries with keep-alive. Recommend increasing MaxIdleConnsPerHost and ResponseHeaderTimeout and align context deadlines.

nate: Another vector: older SDK v0.12 had a bug where retries didn't check ctx.Err() between attempts (GH #4823). We fixed in v0.13 to abort retries when context canceled. Suggest upgrade.

eng-oncall-bot: [deploy] rolled patch 'sdk-go: stop retries after ctx canceled' to staging (deploy/4678) at 2026-02-11T03:12:00Z

eli: Repro suggestion for support: run a small loop with a server that sleeps 8s before writing headers, set ResponseHeaderTimeout=6s and per-request ctx=10s to see Transport timeout; then set ctx=5s to see context cancel race. Should surface 'net/http: request canceled' vs 'response header timeout'.

jordan: Proposed customer action items:
- Upgrade SDK to v0.13.0
- Increase Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout to >= expected backend latency (eg 15s)
- Increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost to 100
- Prefer context-based timeouts per request (but ensure ctx > ResponseHeaderTimeout)

jordan: I'll ask them to test and report back. If still failing we'll collect pprof and tcpdump.
